newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD shares transferred to new owners.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD shares transferred to new owners.

text.p: A controlling stake in privatized Brazilian mining giant CVRD has been transferred to its new owners after a last minute attempt to prevent the transaction in the courts was thrown out.

Valepar, the international consortium led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN, emerged as the winning bidder from the May 6 privatization auction of CVRD, offering $3.15 billion for 41.73 percent of the company's voting stock.
"The share transfer took place this morning on the Rio stock exchange," said a spokesman for Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which oversees Brazil's privatization program.
A Rio de Janeiro court overturned late last night an injunction which suspended the outcome of the privatization auction and blocked payment and share transfer.
The injunction had been issued on the day of the auction itself only minutes before the hammer went down on Latin America's biggest privatization deal.
Legal challenges dogged the CVRD sell-off from the start and managed to delay the auction one week from the original April 29 sale date.

Valepar, which includes CSN, NationsBank Corp, four local pension funds and Opportunity Asset Management's offshore investment fund with investors like Citicorp and George Soros, will be meeting Monday to discuss its next moves.
The composition of CVRD's board of directors and a new management team for the company are the most urgent matters to be decided by Valepar.

A CVRD shareholder meeting is slated to vote Monday at 1500 local time/1400 EDT/1800 GMT on the new board of directors presented by Valepar. Another meeting will be called to vote on CVRD's new management.

Valepar will also be deciding whether to admit as new members of the consortium pension fund Valia and CVRD's employees in conjunction with BNDESpar, the investment arm of BNDES, which would increase its stake in CVRD, a CSN spokesman said.
"Talks are being held with the employees, BNDESpar and Valia, but it's not certain yet whether they will join," he said. "This will be decided on Monday."
Valia owns 1.6 percent of CVRD voting shares, BNDESpar holds 3.24 percent and CVRD employees have the right to acquire 4.45 percent of voting shares under the privatization rules.

In addition, the four pension funds in Valepar also have a joint voting stake in CVRD of 10.03 percent, which means that the consortium's controlling stake would be increased to 61.05 percent of voting shares if the new members are admitted.
